subject: physics

items.q: A car is slowing down as it brakes. What is true about its acceleration?
items.correct: It is accelerating — acceleration is any change in velocity, here negative.
items.misconception: It has no acceleration because it is not speeding up.
items.random_wrong: Its acceleration is zero because braking removes all forces.
items.why: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second, in any direction. Slowing down is a negative acceleration; only constant velocity gives zero.

items.q: A skydiver is falling at terminal velocity. What are the forces?
items.correct: Weight and air resistance are equal and opposite, so the resultant force is zero.
items.misconception: No force acts, which is why the speed stays constant.
items.random_wrong: Weight has disappeared, so only air resistance acts.
items.why: Constant velocity means balanced forces, not no forces. Weight still acts; air resistance has grown to equal it, giving zero resultant.

items.q: What does friction do when you walk forwards?
items.correct: Friction from the ground pushes you forwards — without it your foot would slip back.
items.misconception: Friction only ever slows you down, so it opposes walking.
items.random_wrong: Friction acts downwards to hold you on the ground.
items.why: Friction opposes sliding. Your foot pushes back on the ground, so friction on your foot points forwards and propels you — grip needs friction.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Forces & Motion
